sentences.zh: 如果你读记者的报道，到处都是这些情况，他们会和内阁大臣共进午餐，而部长会开怀畅饮一整瓶

sentences.en: And there are all these, you know, if you read journalists' accounts, they will go for lunch with a cabinet minister and the minister would, you know, they'd happily drink a bottle
sentences.zh: 葡萄酒，饭后再来几小杯烈酒。

sentences.en: of wine and a couple of snifters afterwards.
sentences.zh: 然后起身给国际货币基金组织打电话。

sentences.en: And then go off and phone the IMF.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Just to leave themselves into the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了把时间留到下午。

sentences.en: So I think British politics in the mid-70s feels like a very dandruff-flecked, tired, cynical, and frankly, alcohol-soaked environment.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得70年代中期的英国政坛，给人的感觉是一个满头头皮屑、疲惫、愤世嫉俗，而且坦白说，充满酒精味的环境。

sentences.en: But what's also going on in number 10 under Wilson is this much more sort of baroque soap opera.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，在威尔逊领导下的首相府里，还上演着更具巴洛克风格的肥皂剧。

sentences.en: So to give you a sense of this, on the first full day, he has lunch with his aides, Harold
sentences.zh: 为了让大家有个概念，在上班的第一整天，他和助手们一起吃午饭，哈罗德

sentences.en: Wilson, number 10, and it's all fine.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊，在首相府，一切都很好。

sentences.en: He's very pleased because it's English food.
sentences.zh: 他非常高兴，因为是英国菜。

sentences.en: Wilson is a bit of a nationalist when it comes to food.
sentences.zh: 说起吃的，威尔逊有点大国沙文主义者的倾向。

sentences.en: He doesn't approve of French cheese, for example.
sentences.zh: 比方说，他看不惯法国奶酪。

sentences.en: Then the second day, day two, they go to lunch and it's all recorded in Bernard Donoghue's diary.
sentences.zh: 然后到了第二天，第二天，他们去吃午饭，这一切都被伯纳德·多诺霍的日记记录了下来。

sentences.en: He says, terrible lunch.
sentences.zh: 他说，可怕的午饭。

sentences.en: We all go upstairs to the small dining room.
sentences.zh: 我们都上楼去小餐厅。

sentences.en: We discuss the central policy review staff and appointment.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了中央政策审查小组和任命问题。

sentences.en: Suddenly, Marcia blows up, already upset because we were eating whitebait.
sentences.zh: 突然，玛西亚爆发了，她本来就很心烦，因为我们在吃银鱼。

sentences.en: She says she hates them looking at her from the plate.
sentences.zh: 她说她讨厌它们在盘子里看着她。

sentences.en: The PM solemnly announced that they were from the home for blind whitebait, so she need not worry.
sentences.zh: 首相严肃地宣布它们来自失明银鱼之家，所以她不用担心。

sentences.en: That broke the tension for a while, but then she blew up over Harold and me having a polite and friendly conversation together.
sentences.zh: 这暂时打破了紧张气氛，但接着她又因为哈罗德和我进行礼貌友好的交谈而大发雷霆。

sentences.en: She said it was disgraceful.
sentences.zh: 她说这太无耻了。

sentences.en: She stalked out.
sentences.zh: 她气冲冲地走了出去。

sentences.en: H.W., that's Harold Wilson, the prime minister, followed his meal unfinished.
sentences.zh: H.W.，也就是首相哈罗德·威尔逊，饭也没吃完就跟了出去。

sentences.en: Gloom.
sentences.zh: 一片阴霾。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, Marcia.
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，玛西亚是谁？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Who is Marcia?
sentences.zh: 玛西亚是谁？

sentences.en: So, Marcia Williams is the daughter of a Northamptonshire builder who had started working for the Labour
sentences.zh: 所以，玛西亚·威廉姆斯是北安普敦郡一名建筑工人的女儿，她在20世纪50年代开始为工

sentences.en: Party in the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 党工作。

sentences.en: She'd been introduced to Harold Wilson and they'd become very close and she basically became his private secretary, his absolutely indispensable right hand.
sentences.zh: 她被介绍认识了哈罗德·威尔逊，两人关系变得非常密切，她基本上成了他的私人秘书，他绝对不可或缺的得力助手。

sentences.en: She's the guardian of access to Wilson.
sentences.zh: 她是控制接触威尔逊的门槛的守门人。

sentences.en: She does his paperwork.
sentences.zh: 她帮他处理文件。

sentences.en: She is, I mean, effectively.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她实际上就是。

sentences.en: Well, she is his political wife.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她就是他的政治妻子。

sentences.en: She is his political wife.
sentences.zh: 她就是他的政治妻子。

sentences.en: So, this is the woman that we talked about at the start of the show.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我们在节目开头谈到的那个女人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, Mary Wilson hated politics, thought that her husband was going to be an Oxford economics don and was gutted that he actually went into politics in the first place and made it
sentences.zh: 所以，玛丽·威尔逊讨厌政治，原本以为她丈夫会成为牛津大学的经济学导师，对他在最初选择从政感到极度失望，并且

sentences.en: very clear that she was never really going to take any interest in it or do anything but the bare minimum.
sentences.zh: 明确表示她绝不会对政治产生任何兴趣，也不会做任何超出最低限度的事情。

sentences.en: So, Wilson, from the 50s onwards, has had almost like this sort of second wife.
sentences.zh: 所以，从50年代开始，威尔逊的生活中几乎就一直有这样一位“二房”。

sentences.en: So, they travel as a trio.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们三人总是形影不离地出行。

sentences.en: You know, Marcia is always there in the background.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，玛西亚总是默默地待在背景里。

sentences.en: She is the person who sits up late with him at night.
sentences.zh: 她就是那个晚上陪他熬夜到很晚的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, I mean, just to be clear what that means, again, to quote you, Wilson himself once claimed that after a particularly blazing row, Marcia had gone to see his wife, Mary,
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，为了搞清楚这意味着什么，再次引用你的话，威尔逊本人曾声称，在一次格外激烈的争吵之后，玛西亚曾去找他的妻子玛丽

sentences.en: and announced, I have only one thing to say to you.
sentences.zh: 并宣称，我只有一句话要对你说。

sentences.en: I went to bed with your husband six times in 1956 and it wasn't satisfactory.
sentences.zh: 我在1956年和你丈夫上过六次床，感觉并不令人满意。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 好吧，是的。

sentences.en: Quite an odd relationship.
sentences.zh: 这段关系真够奇特的。

sentences.en: Yeah, very odd relationship.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常奇特的关系。

sentences.en: She would also say to the other aides, when they were having a big row, she would hold up her handbag and tap her handbag meaningfully.
sentences.zh: 每当他们发生大争吵时，她也会对其他助手说，她会举起自己的手袋，意味深长地拍拍手袋。

sentences.en: And she would say, one call to the Daily Mail and he'll be finished.
sentences.zh: 并且她会说，只要给《每日邮报》打一个电话，他就彻底完了。

sentences.en: I will destroy him.
sentences.zh: 我会毁了他。

sentences.en: But she never says, you know, what the information is.
sentences.zh: 但她从来不说，你知道的，那究竟是什么信息。

sentences.en: No, what's in the handbag?
sentences.zh: 不，手袋里装的是什么？

sentences.en: Tom, what's in the handbag?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，手袋里装的是什么？

sentences.en: No one ever knows.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人知道。

sentences.en: And the thing about did they have a physical relationship?
sentences.zh: 至于他们是否有过肉体关系这件事？

sentences.en: I think there is a sense that possibly they did.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有一种感觉，他们可能确实有过。

sentences.en: I mean, this is pure gossip and prurience to speculate whether they did or not, because it doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，猜测他们有没有过纯粹是八卦和窥阴癖，因为这其实并不重要。

sentences.en: What matters is the intensity of the emotional relationship, which is undeniable.
sentences.zh: 重要的是他们之间那种不可否认的情感关系的强度。

sentences.en: But there's something kind of slightly dominatrix about her, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 但她身上有一种略带女施虐狂的特质，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, again, reading you, she demands submission and obedience from Wilson.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，再次读你的书，她要求威尔逊对她顺从和服从。

sentences.en: She does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Now, especially to our listeners who are not British or who are younger and don't remember this period at all and have no knowledge of it, all this will sound very weird.
sentences.zh: 现在，尤其是对我们的听众来说，如果他们不是英国人，或者比较年轻，对这段时期完全没有记忆，也不了解，这一切听起来会非常诡异。

sentences.en: But to give you a sort of sense, so we talked about day two and the white bait bust up.
sentences.zh: 但为了让你有个概念，我们之前谈到了第二天以及银鱼争吵事件。

sentences.en: On day three, there was another massive row at lunch in number 10 Downing Street.
sentences.zh: 在第三天，唐宁街10号的午餐时又爆发了一场大争吵。

sentences.en: At the end of the meal, Marcia walks out in a temper.
sentences.zh: 饭局结束时，玛西亚气冲冲地走了出去。

sentences.en: HW was clearly upset.
sentences.zh: HW显然很不高兴。

sentences.en: She had attacked him viciously in front of the waiter.
sentences.zh: 她当着侍者的面恶毒地攻击了他。

sentences.en: And then she goes straight home.
sentences.zh: 然后她直接回了家。

sentences.en: And Donoghue, the policy guy, has to ring her up past midnight and beg her to come back.
sentences.zh: 负责政策的家伙多诺霍不得不深夜过零点打电话哀求她回来。

sentences.en: She's very depressed and neurotic.
sentences.zh: 她非常沮丧且神经质。

sentences.en: She says, we're all out for ourselves.
sentences.zh: 她说，我们所有人都是为了自己。

sentences.en: We're ganging up against her.
sentences.zh: 我们在合伙对付她。

sentences.en: And I'm out to replace her.
sentences.zh: 而我则是想取代她。

sentences.en: She says she'll retire to her country home and wait for HW to sack us all.
sentences.zh: 她说她要退隐到乡下的家，等着HW把我们全都解雇。

sentences.en: And then he'll have to come personally to ask if she'll return.
sentences.zh: 然后他必须亲自来求她回去。

sentences.en: Now, this may sound madly histrionic, but I can't exaggerate how much time in any given day
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能疯狂地矫情，但我怎么强调都不为过，在任何特定的一天里

sentences.en: Harold Wilson and his chief advisors are spending on this issue.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·威尔逊和他的高级顾问们在这件事上花费了多少时间。

sentences.en: I mean, it comes up again and again.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这问题一而再、再而三地出现。

sentences.en: And so, Dominic, what solution do Wilson's advisors come up with to this problem?
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，威尔逊的顾问们想出了什么解决办法来应对这个问题？

sentences.en: That Marcia is basically dominating all their concerns in the midst of Britain's worst post-war crisis.
sentences.zh: 在英国经历二战后最严重危机的当口，玛西亚基本上主导了他们所有的心力。

sentences.en: Well, unbelievably, Tom, the opening weeks, so when they've returned in March 1974,
sentences.zh: 嗯，难以置信的是，汤姆，在最初的几周里，也就是当他们在1974年3月回归时，

sentences.en: much of their time in the opening weeks is spent on very serious top-level negotiations about who will be allowed to have lunch.
sentences.zh: 他们最初几周的大部分时间都花在了关于谁被允许吃午饭的极其严肃的顶级谈判上。

sentences.en: And the agreement is finally reached.
sentences.zh: 最终达成了协议。

sentences.en: She basically says, Wilson must eat lunch on his own.
sentences.zh: 她基本上规定，威尔逊必须一个人吃午饭。

sentences.en: He is not allowed to eat lunch with his aides.
sentences.zh: 他不被允许和助手们一起吃午饭。

sentences.en: She goes mad if she finds out they've eaten lunch with him.
sentences.zh: 如果她发现他们和威尔逊一起吃过午饭，她就会发疯。

sentences.en: There's a wonderful description in Donoghue's diary.
sentences.zh: 多诺霍的日记里有一段精彩的描述。

sentences.en: Harold was pleading for food, for sandwiches, but Marcia insisted that he sign her letters before he got his sandwiches.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德在恳求给点吃的，给点三明治，但玛西亚坚持要他在拿到三明治之前先在她的信件上签字。

sentences.en: But there is worse.
sentences.zh: 但还有更糟的。

sentences.en: There is far worse.
sentences.zh: 还有糟糕得多的时候。

sentences.en: It is mind-boggling.
sentences.zh: 这简直匪夷所思。

sentences.en: And if you think Boris Johnson was the first prime minister to run a ludicrous and chaotic ship in Downing Street, you'll be very surprised by this.
sentences.zh: 如果你以为鲍里斯·约翰逊是在唐宁街搞出一个荒谬混乱摊子的第一位首相，那你对这个一定会感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: So, first of all, they've obviously won the election unexpectedly.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先，他们显然出人意料地赢得了大选。

sentences.en: And they decide they're going to have a victory party.
sentences.zh: 他们决定举办一场庆祝胜利的派对。

sentences.en: Now, Bernard Donoghue was a lecturer at the London School of Economics.
sentences.zh: 现在，伯纳德·多诺霍是伦敦政治经济学院的一名讲师。

sentences.en: So, he has to go back to give one last lecture before he can kind of come in in a sort of Henry Kissinger-style way.
sentences.zh: 所以，他必须回去上最后一堂课，然后才能以某种亨利·基辛格式的风格加入政府。

sentences.en: He's come from academia to politics.
sentences.zh: 他从学术界来到了政坛。

sentences.en: So, he goes off to give a last lecture, thinking the party is this evening at 8.30.
sentences.zh: 于是他去上最后一课，以为派对是在今晚8点半举行。

sentences.en: And he and his wife, Carol, turn up at 8.30 at Number 10 Downing Street.
sentences.zh: 他和妻子卡罗尔在8点半准时出现在唐宁街10号。

sentences.en: But actually, behind his back that afternoon, Marcia has cancelled the party in a rage.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，就在那天下午他背着身的时候，玛西亚在暴怒中取消了派对。

sentences.en: So, when he and his wife arrive, they're the only people there.
sentences.zh: 所以，当他和妻子到达时，他们是那里仅有的人。

sentences.en: And Wilson greets them, very sheepish and shamefaced, and actually says to them,
sentences.zh: 威尔逊迎接了他们，显得十分局促和羞愧，甚至对他们说，

sentences.en: Oh, hello.
sentences.zh: 哦，你好。

sentences.en: He says, it's all a pantomime.
sentences.zh: 他说，这完全是一场滑稽戏。

sentences.en: It's a riot, quite chaotic.
sentences.zh: 简直是一团糟，相当混乱。

sentences.en: Nobody outside would believe it.
sentences.zh: 外面的人根本不会相信。

sentences.en: A total pantomime.
sentences.zh: 简直是一场闹剧。

sentences.en: I mean, for him to say this about his own administration.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他竟然这样评价自己的政府。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, at least he's self-aware.
sentences.zh: 好吧，至少他还有点自知之明。

sentences.en: And he has a drink with them.
sentences.zh: 他陪他们喝了一杯。

sentences.en: And Marcia rings up half-fifth of the evening and gives him a 40-minute rollicking on the phone.
sentences.zh: 而玛西亚在傍晚快五点时打来电话，在电话里对他破口大骂了40分钟。

sentences.en: For having a drink.
sentences.zh: 就因为喝了杯酒。

sentences.en: For having a drink with Donoghue.
sentences.zh: 就因为和多诺霍喝了杯酒。

sentences.en: And is this kind of jealousy of his aides?
sentences.zh: 这是一种对他的助手们的嫉妒吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Jealousy of the other aides.
sentences.zh: 对其他助手的嫉妒。

sentences.en: But, of course, the most eye-catching story, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，最引人注目的故事，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, this will have to be bleeped out.
sentences.zh: 所以这段到时候得消音处理。

sentences.en: So, we're in the middle of the economic crisis.
sentences.zh: 当时我们正处于经济危机的水深火热之中。

sentences.en: And she tells Harold Wilson that she wants him to come with her to a reception at the House of Lords.
sentences.zh: 她告诉哈罗德·威尔逊，她要他跟她一起去上议院参加一个招待会。

sentences.en: He goes to the reception.
sentences.zh: 他去了招待会。

sentences.en: This is the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 这位可是大不列颠及北爱尔兰联合王国首相。
zh_words: 大不列颠及北爱尔兰联合王国

sentences.en: But he and his speechwriter, Joe Haynes, sneak off from the reception to get back to Number 10 Downing Street to do some work.
sentences.zh: 但他和他的演讲稿撰写人乔·海恩斯从招待会上偷偷溜走，赶回唐宁街10号处理一些工作。

sentences.en: She comes back to Number 10 because she's spotted that he's missing from the reception.
sentences.zh: 她回到10号是因为她发现他在招待会上不见了。

sentences.en: And in full view of everybody there, the staff, she shouts at him, you little ****, what do you think you're doing?
sentences.zh: 在现场所有人的众目睽睽之下，在全体工作人员面前，她对大喊道：“你这个小混蛋，你以为你在干什么？”

sentences.en: You come back with me at once.
sentences.zh: 你马上跟我回去。

sentences.en: And did he go back with her?
sentences.zh: 然后他跟她回去了吗？

sentences.en: And he went back?
sentences.zh: 而他真的回去了？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That does seem quite a kind of psycho-sexual dominatrix kind of thing going on there.
sentences.zh: 那里面确实有点心理性欲色彩的女施虐狂的味道。

sentences.en: So, Joe Haynes, who is his speechwriter, who was a very kind of hard-bitten man, a former newspaper man, he wrote in his memoirs about this.
sentences.zh: 所以，乔·海恩斯，他的演讲稿撰写人，是一个非常坚强老练的人，曾当过报人，他在回忆录中写到了这件事。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, I was frankly very shocked at this, that you could speak to the Prime Minister like this in front of everybody.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，坦白说我对此感到非常震惊，你竟然可以当着所有人的面这样跟首相说话。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it is shocking.
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，这确实很令人震惊。

sentences.en: I mean, it's frankly very odd.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，坦白说这非常怪异。

sentences.en: It is very odd.
sentences.zh: 这确实非常怪异。

sentences.en: I mean, it's inconceivable that somebody would have spoken like this to Ted Heath.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，根本不可想象有人会这样对特德·希斯说话。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, all this psychodrama is going on in Number 10 and monopolising Wilson's attention.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有这些内心戏都在10号上演，并且独占了威尔逊的注意力。

sentences.en: But meanwhile, there is a country in crisis to run.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，还有一个处于危机中的国家需要治理。

sentences.en: So, how are things getting on out on the streets, out in the country?
sentences.zh: 那么，外面的街道上、国家内部的情况怎么样了？

sentences.en: Well, you will remember that the miners are out on strike.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你还记得矿工们正在罢工。

sentences.en: So, the first thing that Harold Wilson does when he comes back is he settles with the miners.
sentences.zh: 所以，哈罗德·威尔逊回来后做的第一件事就是与矿工达成妥协。

sentences.en: So, within days, the guy who's got to take charge of industrial relations, who our British listeners will recognise the name, Michael Foote, a sort of pamphleteer,
sentences.zh: 因此，几天之内，负责劳资关系的那个人——我们的英国听众会认出这个名字——迈克尔·富特，一个某种小册子作家，

sentences.en: a radical pamphleteer, a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 一个激进的小册子作家、记者。

sentences.en: Great enthusiast for Byron.
sentences.zh: 拜伦的超级狂热崇拜者。

sentences.en: Great enthusiast for Byron.
sentences.zh: 拜伦的超级狂热崇拜者。

sentences.en: A very erudite man, but not really one of life's natural administrators.
sentences.zh: 一个博学多才的人，但实在算不上生活中的天生管理者。

sentences.en: He's been put in because the unions know he'll basically give them what they want.
sentences.zh: 他被安排这个职位是因为工会知道他基本上会给他们想要的东西。

sentences.en: And he does.
sentences.zh: 而他也确实做到了。

sentences.en: He gave the miners a wage settlement.
sentences.zh: 他给矿工们谈妥了一份薪资协议。

sentences.en: They, you will remember, had asked for 35%.
sentences.zh: 大家应该还记得，他们之前要求涨薪35%。

sentences.en: Foote gave them 32%, a wage settlement worth £108 million.
sentences.zh: 福特给他们涨了32%，这是一份价值1.08亿英镑的薪资协议。

sentences.en: So, that's double what Ted Heath was offering them.
sentences.zh: 所以，这相当于泰德·希思当时开出条件的两倍。

sentences.en: He basically bribes them to go back to work if you were being harsh.
sentences.zh: 如果说得刻薄一点，他基本上就是在花钱贿赂他们回去工作。

sentences.en: Now, what the Labour Party have done is they have a policy called the social contract.
sentences.zh: 现在，工党采取的做法是实施一项名为“社会契约”的政策。

sentences.en: So, fans of Jean-Jacques Rousseau will enjoy this policy.
sentences.zh: 所以，让·雅克·卢梭的粉丝们一定会喜欢这项政策。

sentences.en: And what this involves is they say, listen, we will give the unions all kinds of goodies.
sentences.zh: 而这涉及的内容是，他们会说，听着，我们会给工会各种各样的大礼包。

sentences.en: So, you'll get improved health and safety.
sentences.zh: 比如，你们会获得更好的健康和安全保障。

sentences.en: You'll get anti-discrimination laws.
sentences.zh: 你们会获得反歧视法律。

sentences.en: You will get better pensions.
sentences.zh: 你们会得到更好的养老金。

sentences.en: You will get better sick pay.
sentences.zh: 你们会得到更好的病假工资。

sentences.en: And the quid pro quo is that if we give you all these treats, you will not keep asking for more money.
sentences.zh: 而作为交换条件，如果我们给你们所有这些好处，你们就不能一直吵着要更多钱。

sentences.en: You know, it's a contract, effectively.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这实际上就是一份契约。

sentences.en: And is this a legally enforceable contract?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是一份具有法律强制力的契约吗？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 完全不是。

sentences.en: It depends on the unions doing their bit.
sentences.zh: 这全看工会能否尽到他们自己的本分。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And also, as we described before, there are hundreds of trade unions.
sentences.zh: 而且正如我们之前所说，这里有数以百计的工会。

sentences.en: They're very competitive with each other.
sentences.zh: 它们之间竞争非常激烈。

sentences.en: They're always trying to outbid each other.
sentences.zh: 它们总是试图在竞价上压倒对方。

sentences.en: So, actually, the people who run the union movement or sort of preside over it.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，那些领导工会运动或者说主持大局的人……

sentences.en: So, Len Murray, who's the head of the Trade Union Congress, he had said to Wilson, you know, deep down, actually, we won't really be able to deliver on our side of this bargain.
sentences.zh: 比如工会大会的负责人伦·默里，他曾对威尔逊说，你知道的，其实在内心深处，我们根本无法兑现我们在这次协议中承诺的这一部分。

sentences.en: Joe Gormley, the leader of the miners, had said to him, don't put us in a false position.
sentences.zh: 矿工领袖乔·戈姆利也曾对他说，别把我们放在虚假的立场上。

sentences.en: And I quote, our role in society is to look after our members, not to run the country.
sentences.zh: 原话是，我们在社会中的角色是照顾我们的会员，而不是治理国家。

sentences.en: But the social contract was good politics.
sentences.zh: 但“社会契约”是一项出色的政治策略。

sentences.en: It made it sound like they had a solution to the problem of high inflation.
sentences.zh: 它听起来像是他们有办法解决高通胀的问题。

sentences.en: But also, Michael Foote is an incredible romantic, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，迈克尔·福特是个极其浪漫主义的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, he really believes it.
sentences.zh: 所以，他是真的深信不疑。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Oh, Michael Foote, like a lot of people at that time, he had two things.
sentences.zh: 哦，迈克尔·福特就像当时很多人一样，有两个特点。

sentences.en: One was, I would argue, they completely misunderstood the ability of the trade union leaders and willingness of the trade union leaders to deliver on promises to government.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是，我认为，他们完全误解了工会领袖履行对政府承诺的能力以及他们愿意这样做的意愿。

sentences.en: They ignored the union leaders when the union leaders said, don't ask of us something we can't deliver.
sentences.zh: 当工会领袖明确表示“不要向我们索取我们办不到的事情”时，他们却选择无视。

sentences.en: But secondly, they have this incredibly rose-tinted, romantic idea of trade unions and all of this kind of thing,
sentences.zh: 但其次，他们对工会以及诸如此类的事情抱有一种极其天真浪漫、戴着玫瑰色眼镜的想法。

sentences.en: which actually people who are closer to the union movement will often say, you know, you're being very starry-eyed and silly about this.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，那些更贴近工会运动的人经常会说，你们在这件事上真是太天真、太可笑了。

sentences.en: They are hard-nosed negotiators.
sentences.zh: 他们是精明的谈判专家。

sentences.en: They will ask for the best deal possible.
sentences.zh: 他们会索取尽可能最好的协议。

sentences.en: Doesn't one of the trade union leaders compare the government to a slot machine in Vegas where they're just pouring money out all the time?
sentences.zh: 难道没有一个工会领袖把政府比作拉斯维加斯的的老虎机，源源不断地往外吐钱吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the postman's leader, Tom Jackson.
sentences.zh: 对，就是邮政工人领袖汤姆·杰克逊。

sentences.en: The postman's leader, yeah.
sentences.zh: 邮政工人的领袖，没错。

sentences.en: The gigantic Las Vegas slot machine that got stuck in favor of the customer.
sentences.zh: 那个因为卡住而一直疯狂偏袒顾客的巨型拉斯维加斯老虎机。

sentences.en: Well, because actually, if you look at what they gave them, the power workers got a 31% deal.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为事实上，如果你看看他们给出的待遇，电力工人获得了31%的涨薪协议。

sentences.en: The civil servants got 32%.
sentences.zh: 公务员获得了32%。

sentences.en: The doctors, 35%.
sentences.zh: 医生获得了35%。

sentences.en: The docker's 30%.
sentences.zh: 码头工人获得了30%。

sentences.en: So wages go up by about a third in the course of 1974.
sentences.zh: 所以在1974年期间，工资大约上涨了三分之一。

sentences.en: And the weird thing is that each time a given trade union leader would go into number 10, have his beer and sandwiches, actually smoked salmon and white wine,
sentences.zh: 诡异的是，每当某个工会领袖走进唐宁街10号，喝着啤酒和三明治——实际上是烟熏三文鱼和白葡萄酒——

sentences.en: and then he'd come out with his massive pay settlement for his members.
sentences.zh: 然后带着为会员争取到的巨额薪资协议走出来时，

sentences.en: He would say on the way out often to the government, you can't keep doing this.
sentences.zh: 他在离开的路上往往会对政府说，你们不能再这样下去了。

sentences.en: I mean, this is mad.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: You can't keep giving me all this money.
sentences.zh: 你们不能再一直给我这么多钱了。

sentences.en: But in private, of course.
sentences.zh: 但私底下，当然又是另一回事了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And because the oil crisis is ongoing.
sentences.zh: 而且因为石油危机仍在持续。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, a bit like we've been going through with Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这有点像我们最近在乌克兰危机中经历的那样。

sentences.en: There's this massive spike.
sentences.zh: 出现了巨大的价格飙升。

sentences.en: So inflation is going up everywhere across the world.
sentences.zh: 所以全世界的通货膨胀都在加剧。

sentences.en: But is it now starting to go up much further in Britain than anywhere else?
sentences.zh: 但是现在英国的通胀率是不是比其他任何地方都要飙升得更高？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This is the thing.
sentences.zh: 问题就在这里。

sentences.en: Every Western European country is facing similar probleMs.
sentences.zh: 每一个西欧国家都面临着类似的问题。

sentences.en: Indeed, every developed country because of the massive spike in oil prices.
sentences.zh: 确切地说，由于石油价格的暴涨，每个发达国家都面临着同样的问题。

sentences.en: However, within about a year of the Western government coming in, as a result of these pay settlements,
sentences.zh: 然而，在西方新政府上台大约一年内，由于这些薪资协议，

sentences.en: prices are going up faster in Great Britain than they are in any other European country by a margin of about five times, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，英国物价上涨的速度比其他任何欧洲国家都要快，差距大约是五倍。

sentences.en: Five times?
sentences.zh: 五倍？

sentences.en: Five times faster in Britain than anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 英国物价上涨的速度比其他任何地方都要快五倍。

sentences.en: God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And as a result of this, because the money is pouring into the economy, the prices of goods are going up as well.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，由于资金大量涌入经济领域，商品价格也随之水涨船高。

sentences.en: So sugar, 184%.
sentences.zh: 所以糖上涨了184%。

sentences.en: Vegetables, 137%.
sentences.zh: 蔬菜上涨了137%。

sentences.en: Even little things, sort of tinned soup, the price goes up by 54%.
sentences.zh: 甚至连一些小东西，比如罐头汤，价格也上涨了54%。

sentences.en: Orange squash, 51%.
sentences.zh: 橙汁饮料上涨了51%。

sentences.en: So this is cost of living crisis on steroids?
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场空前绝后的生活成本危机？

sentences.en: On steroids.
sentences.zh: 空前绝后。

sentences.en: So worse than the one that we've been going through over the past few years, do you think?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得，这比我们过去几年经历的那场还要糟糕吗？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: I would say it depends who you are, right?
sentences.zh: 我想说，这得看你是谁，对吧？

sentences.en: Right, so if you are the power worker who's just got a 35% pay rise.
sentences.zh: 没错，如果你是刚刚获得35%加薪的电力工人。

sentences.en: It's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 那棒极了。

sentences.en: Well, it's not brilliant, actually.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实也谈不上棒极了。

sentences.en: But you're keeping your head above water.
sentences.zh: 但至少你能勉强维持生计。

sentences.en: You're keeping your head above water is what it is.
sentences.zh: 说白了就是能勉强糊口。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: If you're not represented by a trade union, or you're a pensioner on a fixed pension, or you're a student or you're poor, this is unbelievably painful.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有工会代表为你说话，或者你是一个拿着固定养老金的退休人员，又或者你是学生或穷人，这简直痛苦得难以想象。

sentences.en: Because nobody is getting you a pay rise.
sentences.zh: 因为没有人会帮你争取加薪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Or if your union is weak and doesn't have any clout with the government.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你的工会很弱，在政府面前根本没有任何影响力。

sentences.en: So it's at this point that you see a real kind of fracturing, a fraying of, well, I suppose you would say kind of class solidarity or a kind of a sense of national solidarity,
sentences.zh: 所以正是在这个时候，你会看到一种真正的分裂，一种——嗯，我想你会说是某种阶级团结或国家认同感的瓦解和破裂，

sentences.en: because inflation is dividing people into winners and losers.
sentences.zh: 因为通货膨胀把人们分成了赢家和输家。

sentences.en: But also, Dominic, just to say that at this point, class consciousness is really, really important, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，多米尼克，我想说的是，在这个时候，阶级意识真的、真的很重要，对吧？

sentences.en: Much more important than it is now, where there are kind of different ways in which identity is understood today.
sentences.zh: 比现在重要得多，现在人们对身份认同有着各种不同的理解方式。

sentences.en: But back then, it's very much working classes, middle classes, upper classes.
sentences.zh: 但在当年，阶级分化非常明显：工人阶级、中产阶级、上层阶级。

sentences.en: Well, I think the language of class, people are much more comfortable with the language of class, and they fall back on it much more quickly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为关于阶级的语言，人们当时对这种语言要熟悉得多，也更容易顺理成章地使用它。

sentences.en: So I would argue that in the 1970s, certainly people on the left will use the language of class much more quickly and automatically than they would today.
sentences.zh: 所以我敢说，在20世纪70年代，左翼人士肯定会比今天更习惯、更自动地使用阶级语言。

sentences.en: And there was much more a sense of the great conflict in British society being one between classes, whereas I think now, Tom, it's between, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且当时人们更强烈地感觉到，英国社会的主要冲突是阶级之间的冲突，然而我认为现在，汤姆，冲突发生在……

sentences.en: the sort of populists and the elite.
sentences.zh: 民粹主义者和精英阶层之间。

sentences.en: People didn't really talk that way in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 人们在70年代可不怎么那样说话。

sentences.en: They much more talked about the bosses and the working man, you know, people in top hats and people in cloth caps.
sentences.zh: 他们更多谈论的是老板和打工人，你知道的，戴高顶礼帽的人和戴扁帽的人。

sentences.en: People still use that quite dated language of class.
sentences.zh: 人们当时仍然在使用那种相当过时的阶级语言。

sentences.en: I guess people on the left today might be ready to talk about race or sexual identity or whatever than class.
sentences.zh: 我想今天的左翼人士可能更愿意谈论种族、性取向或者诸如此类的话题，而不是阶级。

sentences.en: But those are not issues that are seen as being salient to the same degree back in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 但在70年代，这些并不被视为同等重要或突出的议题。

sentences.en: Would that be fair?
sentences.zh: 这样说公平吗？

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我认为完全正确。

sentences.en: That's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So to give you a sense, just before we go to the break, of what else is going on, Wilson's chancellor is a guy called Dennis Healy.
sentences.zh: 所以为了让你对当时的其他情况有个大致了解，在我们休息一下之前，威尔逊的财政大臣是一个叫丹尼斯·希利的人。

sentences.en: We talked about him last time.
sentences.zh: 我们上次谈到过他。

sentences.en: He'd been in the landings at Anzio.
sentences.zh: 他曾在安齐奥登陆战中服役。

sentences.en: Big eyebrows.
sentences.zh: 长着一对浓眉。

sentences.en: Loves quoting Yeats.
sentences.zh: 酷爱引用叶芝的诗。

sentences.en: Always quoting Yeats and talking about Russian literature.
sentences.zh: 总是满口叶芝的诗句，谈论俄罗斯文学。

sentences.en: He comes in.
sentences.zh: 他上台了。

sentences.en: Healy is a very, in many ways, a very cynical politician.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，希利都是一个非常玩世不恭的政治家。

sentences.en: He says, we'll face a massive economic crisis.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们面临着巨大的经济危机。

sentences.en: On the other hand, we've got a tiny majority.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们的多数优势微乎其微。

sentences.en: There's going to be another election quite soon.
sentences.zh: 很快又要举行另一场大选了。

sentences.en: So actually, we'll just, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，我们只需……你知道的。

sentences.en: Yeah, chuck money at the problem.
sentences.zh: 对，就是砸钱解决问题。

sentences.en: Throw money around.
sentences.zh: 到处挥霍金钱。

sentences.en: Throw fuel on the fire.
sentences.zh: 火上浇油。

sentences.en: So massive new spending on things like pensions and food subsidies and things like this.
sentences.zh: 因此在养老金、食品补贴之类的事情上进行了大量的新支出。

sentences.en: And that's going to be paid for by taxes on the rich.
sentences.zh: 而这笔开支将通过对富人征税来支付。

sentences.en: So we were talking about the pips squeaking.
sentences.zh: 所以我们刚才讨论过让富人痛得嗷嗷叫。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So just to give you a sense of what those taxes are, the higher rate of income tax, Tom, as a representative of the rich yourself, I think you'll find this very painful.
sentences.zh: 为了让你对这些税收有个概念，汤姆，作为富人阶层的代表，我想你会觉得这非常痛苦。

sentences.en: The higher rate of income tax was raised to 83%.
sentences.zh: 更高的个人所得税税率被提高到了83%。

sentences.en: And Tom, I don't know if you have investments, but if you did, the tax rate on the higher rates on your investments would be a very impressive 98%.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我不知道你有没有投资，但如果你有的话，你投资收益的高额税率将会是一个相当惊人的98%。

sentences.en: Goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So this is when the Rolling Stones are going off to south of France and things, is it?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是滚石乐队远走法国南部之类地方的时候吗？

sentences.en: Exactly so.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But not Paul McCartney.
sentences.zh: 但保罗·麦卡特尼没有走。

sentences.en: Paul McCartney stays and does his patriotic duty.
sentences.zh: 保罗·麦卡特尼留下来履行他的爱国职责。

sentences.en: Oh, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，那挺好的。

sentences.en: So Daily Telegraph readers, sort of Middle England, are an absolute and utter meltdown about this.
sentences.zh: 所以《每日电讯报》的读者们，也就是英国本土的中产阶层，对此感到彻底崩溃和抓狂。

sentences.en: And what's compounding all this is that remember, some of our more attentive listeners will remember that the Labour Party have come to office with an incredibly radical manifesto.
sentences.zh: 让情况雪上加霜的是，大家记住——我们一些比较细心的听众会记得——工党带着一份极其激进的宣言上台了。

sentences.en: They're going to set up a national enterprise board to spend billions of pounds a year to buy up British companies and to institute massive state planning.

sentences.en: Whereas Walter Walker is going mad and telling people that he has 13 million recruits, which is about 12,999,999, too many, more than he has.
sentences.zh: 然而沃尔特·沃克却快疯了，告诉别人他有1300万新兵，这大概比他实际拥有的多出了12999999人。

sentences.en: David Sterling is very embarrassed and he goes very quiet after all this comes out.
sentences.zh: 大卫·斯特林感到非常尴尬，这一切曝光后他就变得非常低调。

sentences.en: But obviously, in the minds of people, particularly on the left, this hits home.
sentences.zh: 但很显然，在人们的心目中，特别是左翼人士心中，这留下了深刻印象。

sentences.en: So Harold Wilson is always going on about this with his aides.
sentences.zh: 所以哈罗德·威尔逊总是跟他的助手们喋喋不休地谈论这件事。

sentences.en: Even a couple of years later, they read a story in the newspapers in number 10 that some British mercenaries have been executed in Angola.
sentences.zh: 甚至几年后，他们在首相府里读到报纸上的一个故事，说一些英国雇佣兵在安哥拉被处决了。

sentences.en: And Bernard Donoghue writes in his diary, he was completely taken up with this question of Angolan mercenaries.
sentences.zh: 伯纳德·多诺休在他的日记中写道，他完全被这个安哥拉雇佣兵的问题给占据了心神。

sentences.en: He's genuinely petrified of a right-wing coup in Britain using ex-servicemen as the shock troops.
sentences.zh: 他真的非常害怕英国发生右翼政变，利用退伍军人作为突击部队。

sentences.en: Since there are few troops based in the UK, they could, he believes, carry out a coup d'etat.
sentences.zh: 由于驻扎在英国本土的军队很少，他相信他们能够发动政变。

sentences.en: Now, a man in the pub talking about Angolan mercenaries taking over Britain, that happens.
sentences.zh: 现在，酒吧里的某个家伙谈论安哥拉雇佣兵接管英国，这倒也罢了。

sentences.en: The Prime Minister talking about it is sort of disturbing.
sentences.zh: 首相居然也在谈论这个，就有点令人不安了。

sentences.en: And actually, what all this is, I think, like all the Tony Benn stuff, like all of this,
sentences.zh: 说实话，所有这些，我认为，就像所有关于托尼·本恩的事情一样，就像所有这一切一样，

sentences.en: even to some extent, like the mad histronics about who's having lunch in number 10, all this is clearly a sign of a deep political sickness in Britain in the mid-70s.
sentences.zh: 甚至在某种程度上，就像关于谁在首相府吃午饭的疯狂狂热一样，所有这一切显然都标志着70年代中期英国政治的深重病态。

sentences.en: And I don't think that's me just projecting my own interpretation onto it.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这只是我把自己的解释强加给它。

sentences.en: I think you see that reflected.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以从这些反应中看到这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, it doesn't matter what people in the opposition think, but people within the government itself.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，反对派怎么想并不重要，关键是政府内部的人。

sentences.en: So you're Dennis Healy's, you're Roy Jenkins's, Barbara Castle, Tony Benn, all these people
sentences.zh: 比如丹尼斯·希利、罗伊·詹金斯、芭芭拉·城堡、托尼·本恩，所有这些人

sentences.en: who write diaries and brilliant autobiographies at the time, because they're an exceptionally literate and well-educated group who have taken control of British politics.
sentences.zh: 他们当时写下了日记和精彩的自传，因为他们是一群异常博学、受过良好教育并已经掌控了英国政治的人。

sentences.en: They think something is seriously, deeply wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们认为事情出了严重且深重的问题。

sentences.en: And the question is, can it be turned around?
sentences.zh: 问题是，局势还能扭转吗？

sentences.en: And is Howard Wilson remotely the man to do it, especially as he leads a minority government?
sentences.zh: 哈罗德·威尔逊到底是不是能力挽狂澜的人，尤其是他还领导着一个少数派政府？

sentences.en: And so the tension is sort of mounting and mounting and mounting.
sentences.zh: 所以这种紧张气氛在不断地升级、升级、再升级。

sentences.en: And then on the 18th of September, 1974, Wilson says, okay, fine, let's do this.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1974年9月18日，威尔逊说，好吧，行，我们就这么办。

sentences.en: Let's have a second general election to end the uncertainty and to give the country a definitive direction.
sentences.zh: 让我们举行第二次大选，以结束不确定性，并为国家指明明确的方向。

sentences.en: So he says, I'm going to have a fourth showdown with Ted Heath, winner takes all, to decide the future of the country.
sentences.zh: 所以他说，我将与希思进行第四次对决，胜者通吃，来决定国家的未来。

sentences.en: Tom, an incredible cliffhanger to end the episode.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这一集以一个不可思议的悬念结束了。

sentences.en: So will he manage it?
sentences.zh: 那么他能成功吗？

sentences.en: Will he end up with a larger mandate in his hand?
sentences.zh: 他最终能获得更大的授权吗？

sentences.en: Only one way to find out.
sentences.zh: 只有一个方法可以知道。

sentences.en: And that is by tuning into our next episode, which will be out either tomorrow or if you are a member of the Rest is History Club.
sentences.zh: 那就是收看我们的下一集，它将在明天发布，或者如果你是“历史其余部分”俱乐部的会员。

sentences.en: You've already got it.
sentences.zh: 你已经收到了。

sentences.en: So huge excitement.
sentences.zh: 真是令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There are two ways to find out.
sentences.zh: 有两种方法可以知道。

sentences.en: And in fact, I can't believe that anybody listening to that amazing cliffhanger would not join the Rest is History Club immediately.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我简直不敢相信任何听到那个精彩悬念的人不会立即加入“历史其余部分”俱乐部。

sentences.en: You'd be mad.
sentences.zh: 你会疯掉的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You'd be mad not to.
sentences.zh: 不加入才怪呢。

sentences.zh: 不仅如此，加入“历史其余部分”俱乐部的一大福利是，如果你加入，我们将培训你如何在发生严重的

sentences.en: 1970s-style general strike.
sentences.zh: 20世纪70年代风格的大罢工时运营发电厂。

sentences.en: So exciting.
sentences.zh: 太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.zh: 那么下一集，1974年的第二次大选。
